scene_translation: The station attendant thought for a moment, then said quietly, "That person was right in front of those lockers just now." Without meeting your eyes, he pointed toward the lockers. When you went over to look, you found one locker with its door left open. Inside was a small blue envelope — and written on it were the words: "For テスト."
grammar_note: 【〜てある】is used when someone has done something intentionally and the result remains visible. 「書いてある」means "it has been written (by someone, and is still there)" — focus is on the resulting state, not who did it. Compare: 書いた (someone wrote it) vs. 書いてある (it is written / has been written).

vocab.meaning: honorific title (more formal than さん)
the lock is open / the door is unlocked

mystery_memo: The blue envelope addressed to テスト was waiting inside an unlocked locker — clearly left there on purpose. The woman in blue knew the player's name before any introduction, and prepared this in advance. The station attendant (nervous, avoids eye contact) seems to know more than he's saying; he may have been asked to keep quiet or is simply frightened. The blue envelope is now the central clue — its contents will deepen the mystery in Act 2.
